logo_usage.description: Primary logo is the main/default logo mark.

Two alternate logo versions exist beyond the primary: a horizontal version and a stacked version, giving flexibility across different layouts/formats while maintaining brand consistency (page shows three numbered logo examples).

Always give the logo plenty of breathing room / clear space so it isn't crowded by text, images, or other design elements; this negative space keeps the logo legible and impactful. When in doubt, use more space rather than less. No specific minimum-size or exact clearspace measurement (e.g. in inches/logo-widths) is given in the extracted text.

Do: use the logo so it remains clear, recognizable, and unaltered, maintaining its integrity across designs. Don't: add drop shadows, change the logo's color, stretch it, or place it over busy backgrounds -- these can make it hard to read or stray from brand identity. When in doubt, keep it simple.

voice_and_tone.description: Speak with "we" language and extend credit freely.
Write like a trusted friend, not a gatekeeper.
Stay rooted in the real, tangible impact of creativity in everyday life.
Use straightforward, confident language; emphasize shared action and regional pride; tell real stories and invite participation; reference familiar experiences, community spaces, and real outcomes.
Don't use vague nonprofit jargon or arts elitism; don't overstate institutional credit; don't speak in abstract mission-speak; don't assume the audience has a formal arts background.

Not enough: "We advocate for regional arts initiatives." (too passive, lacks identity/impact). Perfect: "We bring people together to turn bold, creative ideas into real change—on your street, in your school, in your life." (specific, human-centered, rooted in place). Too much: "We facilitate catalytic artistic activation across cross-sector stakeholder environments." (overwritten, impersonal, alienating).

messaging.text: Allied Arts Council connects people, organizations, and ideas to strengthen the role of the arts in Northwest Missouri. Through partnerships, advocacy, and community-driven leadership, we support a thriving creative culture—one that is visible, valued, and vital to the identity of our region.

We envision a region where the arts are woven into everyday life—accessible, celebrated, and deeply valued by people of all ages and backgrounds. Allied Arts Council exists to unite communities, spark creative expression, and lead a movement that makes the arts essential to who we are and how we live in Northwest Missouri.

"Together, We Create" speaks to the heart of the word Allied—a name grounded in collaboration, unity, and shared purpose. This tagline positions AAC as a connector and co-creator, highlighting that the arts in Northwest Missouri thrive through community effort, mutual investment, and collective vision. The tone is approachable, hopeful, and mission-aligned.
Together, We Create Community — We connect people, organizations, and ideas to strengthen cultural identity and civic pride.
Together, We Create Opportunity — The arts are an engine for education, talent retention, tourism, and regional development.
Together, We Create Belonging — Our work makes creative spaces feel welcoming, familiar, and approachable to all.
Together, We Create Momentum — We help artists, organizations, and partners grow stronger—faster—through collective effort.
Together, We Create Expression — We give voice to stories, experiences, and perspectives through the power of the arts.
Together, We Create Movement — We're leading a cultural shift where the arts become part of everyday life.

Collaboration: "We believe in shared success. We create space where artists, leaders, and communities build together." Leadership: "We take initiative with clarity and courage. We champion big ideas that position the arts as a public good." Stewardship: "We care for what we've inherited and invest in what's next. Our decisions are grounded in responsibility."

Three defined audiences with tailored tone/voice approach and example quotes: (1) Local Artists & Arts Organizations — tone: supportive, energizing, collaborative; quote: "You shape our region's creative identity. We're here to amplify your work, not compete with it." (2) Civic Leaders, Donors & Business Community — tone: strategic, visionary, pragmatic; quote: "The arts are not an extra—they're an asset. A smart, visible investment in our region's future." (3) General Public (families, students, visitors, everyday citizens) — tone: approachable, enthusiastic, clear; quote: "You don't have to be an 'artist' to enjoy the arts—this is your space, your stage, your story."
